title: The adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$
statement:
For $f$ admitting a compactification and $\mathcal A$ as in
[def-sfb-finite-shriek-adjunction-compactification], the adjunction

$$
Rf_!\dashv Rf^!
$$

on the unbounded derived categories, between the functors of
[def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek] and [def-sfb-finite-upper-shriek], is the adjunction
of [def-sfb-finite-shriek-adjunction-compactification] for the chosen compactification.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring, let $f\colon X\to Y$ admit a compactification, and let $Y$ be
quasi-compact. For $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ bounded below of étale origin
([def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]) and $L\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ bounded below,
there is a bijection

$$
\Hom(Rf_!K,L)\simeq\Hom(K,Rf^!L),
$$

natural in $K$ and $L$, between the pro-étale $Rf_!$ of [def-sfb-finite-derived-lower-shriek]
and $Rf^!$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-shriek]. Its inverse is $g\mapsto\varepsilon_L\circ Rf_!(g)$
for a counit $\varepsilon_L\colon Rf_!Rf^!L\to L$, natural in $L$. Consequently, for full
subcategories $P$ of the bounded below objects of étale origin on $X$ and $Q$ of the bounded
below objects on $Y$ with $Rf_!P\subseteq Q$ and $Rf^!Q\subseteq P$ (for instance the bounded
constructible objects of finite Tor amplitude), the restrictions of $Rf_!$ and $Rf^!$ are
adjoint.

proof.text:
Write $K=

u_{Y,*}L)
\simeq\Hom(K_0,f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}L)\simeq\Hom(
u_X^*K_0,
u_X^*f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}L).
$$
The first step is the compact-support comparison $Rf_!
u_X^*\simeq
u_Y^*Rf^{\et}_!$ on bounded
below objects, from extension by zero ([lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]) and proper
direct image. The second is the adjunction $
u^*\dashv R
u_*$, the third the étale adjunction
of [thm-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-left-adjoint], and the last the full faithfulness of $
u_X^*$
on bounded below objects ([thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]); here $f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}L$ is
bounded below by [lem-sfb-finite-upper-shriek-bounded-below]. The counit is the image of the
identity of $Rf^!L$, and the restriction to $P$ and $Q$ is formal.
